evidence_items.source_text: At another hospital’s evaluation, initial lab results were: white blood cell counts 6.27 × 10^9/L; mature lymphocyte counts 0.87 × 10^9/L; CD4 + T cell counts: 30/uL; CD8 + T cell counts: 165/uL; CD4/CD8+: 0.18; NK cell counts 56/uL.

Physical examination revealed general severe pitting edema. Mild verrucous hyperplasia was noted in the face and upper extremities, while severe and coalescing lesions were present in lower extremities.

Upon admission, laboratory tests showed: urinary protein 4+, red blood cells 71.9/uL, white blood cells 1.8/uL; 24-hour urine protein 4.5 g; serum albumin 16.5 g/l; serum creatinine 63 µmol/L (corresponding to an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 123 mL/min/1.73 m² as calculated by the CKD-EPI equation); hemoglobin 115 g/L; white blood cell counts 3.68 × 10^9/L; mature lymphocyte counts 0.81 × 10^9/L; platelets were normal. CD4 + T cell counts: 77/Ul (reference range, 441–2156/uL); CD8 + T cell counts: 339/uL (reference range,125–1312/uL); CD4/CD8+: 0.23 (reference range, 0.71–2.78); NK cell counts 49/uL (reference range, 95–640/uL). TSH: 24.90 mIU/L, FT3: 3.44pmol/L, TT4: 53.80nmol/L, thyroglobulin: 52.40ng/Ml. Anti-nuclear antibody 1:100, anti-double-stranded DNA antibody with titer of 25.4/IU. All extractable nuclear antigen (ENA) test were negative. The complement C3 levels were reduced to 0.58 g/L, while complement C4 0.17 g/L was within the normal range. Subsequent investigations disclosed that the serum immunoglobulin G (IgG) concentration was markedly diminished, registering at 4.51 g/L. The assays for anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA), anti-glomerular basement membrane (GBM) antibody, serum anti-M-type phospholipase A2 receptor (PLA2R) antibody, Coombs’test, antiphospholipid antibody, immunofixation electrophoresis, and tumor biomarkers all manifested negative findings. The viral serological screenings for herpes simplex virus (HSV) and rubella virus (RV) exhibited equivocal results. The diagnostic tests for hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), cytomegalovirus (CMV), syphilis, and HIV were all negative. Bone marrow flow cytometry analysis did not identify any conspicuous aberrant hematopoietic lymphocytes and plasma cells. Whole-genome sequencing failed to detect any genetic polymorphisms or mutations.

Ultrasound examination of the kidneys showed showed normalsized kidneys (right 136 × 66 mm; left 123 × 60 mm). Thyroid B-ultrasound: Diffuse thyroid lesions with left lobe and isthmus nodules, TI-RADS category 3.

Combining clinical and lab findings, pathological diagnosis was class V lupus nephritis. The patient met three of the EULAR/ACR 2019 classification criteria for systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) [5]with a total score of 11 including glomerular proteinuria, and a Class V renal biopsy (8). Positive ANA results, and reduced complement C3 proteins (3).
During the one-years follow-up, deep vein embolism, acute kidney injury and cytomegaloviraemia occurred, while the proteinuria showed no remission and the verrucous lesions expanded seriously.

Considering the increasing number of studies reporting the efficacy of belimumab in LN, this drug was added to achieve better disease control, while continuously and closely monitoring the patient for potential adverse events. Surprisingly, after one year, the patient’s renal function improved, proteinuria reached partial remission, lupus activity was mostly subdued, and the warts remained stable, although the CD4⁺T cell count was still less than 150 cells per cubic millimeter (Fig.
evidence_items.temporal_cue: after one year of belimumab treatment

evidence_items.source_text: Based on the patient’s lymphocyte count, comprehensive medical history, clinical manifestations, the entire treatment process, as well as the results of various auxiliary examinations, we arrived at a consideration of a diagnosis of ICL. Additionally, throughout the disease course, the CD4 + T cell count remained persistently below 150 cells/µL, with no improvement observed even when the prednisone dosage was tapered to 7.5 mg per day and lupus activity was nearly quiescent. Therefore, we conclude that the patient’s immunodeficiency is not solely attributable to lupus or long-term corticosteroid use, but rather strongly suggests the presence of ICL.
